reasons: The tests were read but not run during this review.
The rules they check are clearly written and cover failure paths.

terms.meaning: a fake stand-in for a real service that returns canned answers so tests run without outside calls
a shared setup helper that pytest provides to tests
a library that checks that data has the right shape and types before the program uses it
a library that lets async code run under pytest
the person or agent who carries out a step in a process

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports and shared setup
sections.what: Brings in the designer, the schema types, and the stub client used across the tests. It also marks the tests as async so they run on the asyncio runner.
sections.why: Likely reason: tests should run without calling a real model service, so the stub replaces it.
sections.watch_out: The async marker must stay consistent with the anyio_backend fixture, or async tests may not run.

sections.name: anyio_backend
sections.title: Async runner choice
sections.what: Tells the async test runner to use asyncio for these tests.
sections.why: Likely reason: the agent code is written for asyncio.

sections.name: architected
sections.title: Sample architect output
sections.what: Builds a sample architect result with two steps, a purpose, a moderate posture, and citations.
sections.why: Gives the designer a realistic upstream input that it must accept without changing the flow.
sections.watch_out: Many tests compare against these exact step names and citation ids, so changing them changes many results.

sections.name: designed
sections.title: Sample designed agent
sections.what: Builds one sample agent called extractor with a responsibility, a tool, a data contract, and a pattern.
sections.why: Gives the designer a valid agent to return in its output.

sections.name: exception_model
sections.title: Sample exception model
sections.what: Builds sample escalation rules: a trigger, a four hour human response time, and a fallback behaviour.
sections.why: The designer must return an exception model, so tests need a valid example.

sections.name: output
sections.title: Sample designer output
sections.what: Builds a full designer response that uses the given agents and steps, with default steps that match the architect's flow.
sections.why: This is the fake model answer most tests start from.
sections.watch_out: The default steps must keep the architect's names and order, or the success tests will fail for the wrong reason.

sections.name: steps_with_performer
sections.title: Steps with a swapped performer
sections.what: Copies the architect's flow but changes who performs the first step, and can attach an invented citation.
sections.why: Lets tests check that only the performer changes, and that invented citations are caught.

sections.name: TestFlowIntegrity
sections.title: Flow must not change
sections.what: Checks that adding, dropping, or renaming a step is rejected with a message that the flow changed, and that an unchanged flow passes.
sections.why: The designer resolves performers. It must not redesign the process.

sections.name: TestEvidenceLinkage
sections.title: Citations carried forward
sections.what: Checks that the designer must supply its own citation list, and that the final result includes citations from both stages.
sections.why: Each stage's claims need their own sources, and the final design should show both.

sections.name: TestHappyPath
sections.title: Normal successful design
sections.what: Checks that a valid run returns a complete future state, keeps the architect's posture unchanged, keeps human steps as human, and uses the standard model tier.
sections.why: Confirms the normal path works and that the designer does not re-choose the posture.

sections.name: TestBoundary
sections.title: Vendor and pricing refusals
sections.what: Checks that naming a vendor or putting a price in a tool list is refused, that the task text forbids vendors and warns against automating human work, and that the exception model is required.
sections.why: Vendor choice and pricing belong to a separate assessment, and human work must stay human.

sections.name: TestFailurePaths
sections.title: Failure cases
sections.what: Checks that a step done by an agent that was never designed is refused, retried once and then accepted if fixed, that the exception model cannot be left out, and that an invented citation is rejected.
sections.why: Each failure must be caught early rather than producing a design that looks complete but is wrong.

summary: Tests that the agent designer assigns real performers to each step of an already-designed flow, and refuses any change to the flow itself, any vendor naming, and any invented citation.
purpose: Checks the rules of the designer stage: it may resolve who does each step, but it may not redesign the flow, name vendors or prices, or drop human steps.
why: The designer sits between two stages, and each stage must stay in its lane. These tests guard the boundary so a later stage cannot quietly change what an earlier stage decided.
how: It builds sample architect output and sample designer output, then runs the designer against a stub model client. Each test checks that the result is accepted, rejected with a specific message, or retried once. The test names describe the rule being checked.
inputs: Sample architect output, sample designed agents, sample steps, and a stub client that returns canned model answers.
outputs: Pass or fail results for each test. No real model is called.
risks: The tests rely on exact message wording in the errors, so a reword in the code breaks them even when behaviour is right. They also depend on the stub returning answers in order.
debug: If a test fails, read the assertion message first. Check the sample steps match the architect sample, since most tests assume the default steps match. Look at the stub answer order when a retry test fails.
